warning_texts: This profile runs on a single vendor: the architect, every worker, every auditor and this red team are all claude-opus-5. An isolated context is not an independent vendor, so a blind spot the model family shares would pass on both sides of every check, and this PASS/FAIL does not replace cross-vendo

Only the deterministic layer really holds here: the machine gates, the frozen check_plan, the control lock and the release surface gate. The prose blocker at release/report.md line 24 sits exactly where that layer has no rule, which is prose without numerals.

Writes over raw_data and the frozen machinery were closed only by permissions.deny for edit tools, not for the shell, so a modified raw file would be caught by the control lock after the fact, not prevented; I did not verify lock hashes because runner state is outside my inputs.

All five auditor results (gate0_semantic, gate_clean_auditor, gate_metrics_auditor, gate_claims_auditor, gate_release_auditor) have placeholder summaries of the form 'driver e2e <step>', evidence notes with no calculation in them, and created_at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, so their PASS verdicts carry no

All four worker results likewise have placeholder summaries, no disclosures field, empty warnings, and one identical check (the refund rate 0.473684) whatever the stage, so nothing in them says whether any stage deviated from its prompt.

The four worker carries (audit/checkpoints/*.carry.json) pass the carry schema, and their context_id and attempt match each stage's result.json, but their bodies are byte-identical apart from ids. Each defines the population as status=delivered, with the period only in the periods field. None record
Every worker carry lists raw_data/orders.csv under do_not_reread, but common contract rule 26 reserves that field for outputs and working data of the previous stage, which the raw export is not.

Assumption, period end: audit_spec.yaml ends the period on 2025-03-30 while the metrics registry calls it 2025-Q1-delivered and questions.md calls it the reported quarter. No raw row is dated 2025-03-31, so no published number moves today, but if the mandate meant the calendar quarter, a future expo

Assumption, refund_rate_basis = paying_customers: the published 0.473684 (27/57) is 2.50 times the order-row reading of 0.189655 (33/174). audit_spec.yaml calls the difference roughly a factor of three, and risk_register.yaml calls it 2.5x.

Also on the refund basis: 15 of the 27 refunded customers had only partial refunds (some under EUR 20). The rendered caveat says the denominator is customers, not rows, but never says that any partial refund on any one order counts a customer as refunded, and that reading is what drives 0.473684.

Assumption, revenue_recognition = net_of_refunds: each refund is attributed to its order's date, and the export has no refund date. The refund total of 4493.50 behind net revenue 35741.52 may therefore include refunds issued after the quarter, and nothing in the data can confirm or refute that.

Assumption, timezone_for_dates = Europe/Warsaw: order_date carries no time component, so the ruling cannot be tested. The delivered rows on the boundary days (three on 2025-01-01 and one on 2025-03-30, net 458.95 in total) bound what a date-shift error could move in net revenue 35741.52.

The claims_rendered and caveats_rendered rules of gate_release_document appear in check_plan.json accepted_unproven, because the plan proof failed with FileNotFoundError, so their PASS was never shown to fire on a broken input.
